answer: Price identities against an epoch beacon: each epoch, it publishes a sequential memory-hard puzzle whose difficulty scales with identities admitted, so admission costs base*(n+1). Unproven keys may not wander onto the ledger; proofs unbound to the key are rejected. Puppets cannot pre-farm proofs (unpredictable beacon) or mint them in parallel (memory-hard). A sybil buying n identities pays base*((n+1)(n+2)/2), each puppet a rising fee, no bulk discount; honest users pay once. Settled proofs harden like basalt; slashed keys are dead embers that must repay the climb.
